newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco to back part of $1.2bln rail project.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco to back part of $1.2bln rail project.

text.p: San Francisco supervisors agreed Wednesday to provide financial backing for a proposed $1.167 billion rail extension project, city officials said.
The Board of Supervisors approved a resolution that calls for San Francisco to back a lease agreement between the Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) District and the San Francisco International Airport.
The resolution was approved Wednesday by a vote of 6-to-4. Earlier this week, the same measure failed to pass.
The resolution is a crucial part of the proposed 8.7-mile, $1.167 billion project extending BART to San Francisco International, officials said.
Under the resolution, San Francisco will ensure that BART pays its rent in full to the airport. Should BART default on its rent, the city would redirect transit funding to cover the lease payments.
Last week, the San Francisco Airport Commission approved the lease agreement, allowing BART to build rail facilities at the airport for an annual rent of $2.5 million for 50 years.
BART's board will consider the lease agreement Thursday.
